intro_script: Welcome to the Robotics News Digest for November 25, 2026. We've got 16 updates, including news on major acquisitions, humanoid robot programs, and advancements in physical AI. Tune in for the latest!
outro_script: And that's all the circuits for today, November 25th, 2026. SoftBank is adding some serious smarts to the robotic world! Thanks for plugging into the future with us. See you tomorrow!

items.title: SoftBank acquires Marc Raibert’s Robotics and AI Institute
items.summary: SoftBank acquired the Robotics and AI Institute (RAI) from Hyundai Motor Group. RAI was founded by Marc Raibert and focuses on fundamental robotics challenges like mobility, manipulation, and intelligence. The acquisition adds another notable robotics entity to SoftBank's growing portfolio. RAI is currently seeking to expand its team with open positions in various robotics technologies. This move creates potential synergies between RAI's research and other companies within SoftBank's portfolio.
items.audio_script: From The Robot Report, SoftBank acquires Marc Raibert’s Robotics and AI Institute. This report details the acquisition of the Robotics and AI Institute by SoftBank, which adds another significant robotics entity to the conglomerate's portfolio. The acquisition involves SoftBank taking over the Robotics and AI Institute from Hyundai Motor Group. The institute was founded by Marc Raibert and focuses on fundamental robotics challenges including mobility, manipulation, and intelligence. This transaction creates potential synergies between the institute's ongoing research and other entities within SoftBank's investment portfolio. The Robotics and AI Institute is currently seeking to expand its team by filling various open positions across different robotics technologies. This development signals an integration of advanced robotics research into a major technology investment group. The industry should monitor future collaborations arising from this integration.

items.title: Türkiye launches humanoid robot program with 50% grants
items.summary: Türkiye's Industry and Technology Ministry has initiated a program offering 50% grants to develop domestic industrial humanoid robots. The program focuses on bipedal machines for manufacturing assembly, logistics, and precision machining over up to 48 months. Requirements specify robots at least 1.6 meters tall capable of multi-tasking, with specific lifting and mobility specifications. A key objective is to foster domestic development of core components like actuators, sensors, and software architecture. Applications will be evaluated based on innovation, economic value, and social impact.
items.audio_script: From Humanoid.guide, Türkiye launches humanoid robot program with 50% grants. This report details the initiation of a national program offering substantial financial support to develop domestic industrial humanoid robots. The program is specifically focused on bipedal machines intended for manufacturing assembly, logistics, and precision machining, with funding provided at a fifty percent grant rate over a period extending up to forty-eight months. The initiative mandates that developed robots must be at least one point six meters in height and possess multi-tasking capabilities, alongside defined specifications for lifting and mobility. A primary goal of this effort is the domestic development of essential components such as actuators, sensors, and software architecture. Applications submitted for evaluation will be assessed based on demonstrated innovation, economic value, and social impact. This move signals a concentrated effort to build indigenous capabilities within the robotics and artificial intelligence sectors. Further developments in domestic hardware and software solutions are anticipated in the coming months.

items.title: Siemens advances physical AI and autonomous production technologies
items.summary: Siemens is integrating artificial intelligence to enable autonomous production through AI-powered planning, engineering, and physical AI applications on factory floors. The company demonstrates goal-based automation, exemplified by an AI-powered robotic system in their Electronics Factory that autonomously unpacks goods using real-time camera input. Siemens' Autonomous Production Planner uses collaborating AI agents and physics-based digital twins to optimize schedules, potentially reducing manual planning by 70%. Furthermore, the company is enhancing its AI with agents that adapt automation code and integrating AI directly into machine control systems. This development also emphasizes the importance of cybersecurity in industrial AI and supports compliance with regulations like the EU's Cyber Resilience Act.

Siemens is also enhancing its AI by incorporating agents that adapt automation code and integrating artificial intelligence directly into machine control systems, underscoring the need for cybersecurity in industrial AI compliance with regulations such as the European Union's Cyber Resilience Act. This development signals a progression toward fully autonomous industrial environments.

items.title: Roscosmos launches Teledroid humanoid for ISS exterior work
items.summary: Roscosmos launched the Teledroid humanoid robot toward the International Space Station on November 24, 2026, aboard the Progress MS-36. The robot is designed to prepare exterior worksites by opening casings and installing equipment before cosmonauts perform spacewalks. Teledroid will combine operator motion copying with autonomous task execution, controllable from inside the station or ground control. Control hardware, including a workstation, was delivered prior to the robot's launch. Future steps involve crew training and physical installation outside the Nauka module.
items.audio_script: From Humanoid.guide, Roscosmos launches Teledroid humanoid for ISS exterior work. The robot was deployed aboard the Progress MS-36. Teledroid integrates operator motion copying with autonomous task execution, allowing control from within the station or ground control. Control hardware, including a necessary workstation, was delivered before the launch. Future operations will involve crew training and physical installation outside the Nauka module. This development signals advancements in remote manipulation and autonomous robotics for complex extravehicular activities.

items.title: Robotics Summit 2027 opens call for speakers
items.summary: The Robot Report is seeking session abstracts for the 2027 Robotics Summit & Expo, which will take place in Boston on June 2-3. The summit focuses on the technical development of commercial robots, attracting over 5,000 attendees and featuring numerous educational sessions. Session topics are organized into tracks covering technologies, design, AI, coding, logistics, and healthcare robotics. The deadline for submitting speaker proposals is December 30, 2026. All accepted speakers receive complimentary full conference registration.

items.title: Reliability emerges as the next big challenge for robotics
items.summary: Ensuring the reliable, consistent, and safe operation of robots over extended periods is now a major challenge in the robotics industry. Reliability engineering is crucial across diverse applications, including humanoid robots, warehouse automation, robotic surgery, and subsea inspection. Developers are increasingly adopting Design for Reliability methodologies and using engineering software to assess potential system weaknesses early in the development process. Operational data from sensors is also being used to refine designs and maintenance strategies. Ultimately, reliability is becoming a competitive differentiator, determining the success and scalability of future robotics companies.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, "Reliability emerges as the next big challenge for robotics". This report details the growing necessity for ensuring the reliable, consistent, and safe operation of robots over extended periods across various industrial applications. Developers are increasingly integrating Design for Reliability methodologies and employing engineering software to proactively assess system weaknesses during the development phase. Operational data gathered from sensors is being utilized to refine both system designs and subsequent maintenance strategies. This focus on reliability is establishing itself as a critical competitive differentiator determining the success and scalability of future robotics ventures. The industry must prioritize robust reliability engineering to support the advancement of artificial intelligence and automation technologies.

items.title: Researcher develops quantum-inspired approach to safer autonomous drone navigation
items.summary: Dr. Sai Krishna Thota developed a quantum-inspired decision-support framework to enhance the safety and reliability of autonomous drone navigation. This framework prioritizes operational risks alongside conventional route planning objectives, addressing the limitations of shortest-route methods. The system evaluates routes based on factors like energy consumption, weather, and safety requirements. Simulations showed the framework reduced route risk by 20.5% and safety rule violations by 52.8% compared to existing methods. Although a trade-off with energy consumption was noted, the research supports knowledge-based systems for more reliable autonomous navigation.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, researcher develops quantum-inspired approach to safer autonomous drone navigation. This story details the development of a quantum-inspired decision-support framework intended to enhance the safety and reliability of autonomous drone navigation by integrating operational risks into route planning. The research involved creating a system that evaluates potential routes based on a combination of energy consumption, prevailing weather conditions, and established safety requirements, moving beyond simple shortest-route calculations. Simulations demonstrated that this new framework achieved a reduction in route risk by twenty point five percent and a decrease in safety rule violations by fifty-two point eight percent when compared to existing navigation methods. While an increase in energy consumption was observed, the findings support the implementation of knowledge-based systems for more dependable autonomous flight. This work indicates a trajectory toward more robust and safer autonomous aerial systems.

items.title: Bentic prepares for US expansion as physical AI robot installations approach 100
items.summary: Bentic is advancing the commercial use of physical AI in industrial automation, with nearly 100 robots already deployed handling deformable materials. The company's technology enables robots to manage tasks involving textiles, cables, carbon fiber, and food, which have historically resisted conventional automation. Bentic trains its AI using real-world industrial data from production environments rather than solely relying on simulation. Their system combines predictive intelligence with action models to facilitate manipulation of complex materials. Bentic is preparing for US market expansion, aiming to deploy its systems there by the end of 2026.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, Bentic prepares for US expansion as physical AI robot installations approach 100. The company's technology allows robots to manage tasks involving textiles, cables, carbon fiber, and food, materials that have historically resisted conventional automation methods. Bentic achieves this by training its artificial intelligence using real-world industrial data gathered directly from production environments, moving beyond reliance on simulation. The system integrates predictive intelligence with action models to facilitate the manipulation of these complex materials. The company is currently planning for expansion into the United States, targeting the deployment of its systems there by the end of 2026. This development indicates a growing commercial application for physical AI in challenging industrial settings.

items.title: Adcock Answers Musk's Apple Challenge With a Figure 03 Clip
items.summary: Brett Adcock provided a Figure 03 clip demonstrating autonomous task completion after a table was moved. This clip was presented in response to Elon Musk's claim that humanoid robot demonstrations are staged and pre-programmed. Adcock argued that Figure's Helix model achieved zero-shot, fully autonomous performance, allowing the robot to successfully pick up an apple from a relocated table. This capability addresses Musk's broader assertion that no robot can perform arbitrary tasks with unfamiliar objects. Figure AI is also pursuing the goal of robots handling multi-hour chores in any home within six months.
items.audio_script: From Humanoids Daily, Adcock Answers Musk's Apple Challenge With a Figure 03 Clip. This report details a demonstration of autonomous task completion by a humanoid robot following a table relocation. Brett Adcock presented a Figure 03 clip illustrating the robot's ability to successfully pick up an apple from a table that had been moved. The demonstration highlighted that the Figure AI Helix model achieved zero-shot, fully autonomous performance in this scenario, directly addressing claims regarding the limitations of current humanoid robot programming. This achievement suggests a capability for robots to perform arbitrary tasks with unfamiliar objects, aligning with the broader goals of the AI research sector. Further development from Figure AI aims for robots to handle multi-hour chores in any home within six months. This development signals progress toward more general artificial intelligence in physical environments.

items.title: Where eagles dare: XPeng’s physical AI ambitions prepare for take-off
items.summary: XPeng is pursuing physical AI ambitions by developing its own computing hardware, like the Turing AI processor, to run large AI models on-device across vehicles, robots, and flying vehicles. The company views intelligent vehicles as "robots on wheels," integrating AI into physical actions like steering and braking. XPeng is developing a humanoid robot named Iron, which utilizes their AI and computing expertise, indicating a focus on physical AI. This expansion is supported by significant investment, with the robotics business securing substantial financing. The company aims for AI to impact the real world by applying its technology across various physical forms.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, "Where eagles dare: XPeng’s physical AI ambitions prepare for take-off". This report details XPeng's pursuit of physical artificial intelligence through the development of proprietary computing hardware for on-device AI execution across physical systems. XPeng is developing components such as the Turing AI processor to facilitate the running of large artificial intelligence models directly on vehicles, robots, and flying vehicles, conceptualizing intelligent vehicles as robots on wheels that integrate AI into physical operations like steering and braking. Furthermore, the company is developing a humanoid robot named Iron, leveraging its AI and computing strengths to demonstrate a focus on physical AI applications, a development supported by significant investment in the robotics sector. This expansion indicates a strategy to apply advanced AI technology across tangible, real-world forms. The trajectory suggests a growing integration of sophisticated AI into physical automation systems moving forward.

items.title: Neuryn Robotics develops AI-powered robots to automate fashion returns
items.summary: Neuryn Robotics, a Madrid startup, is developing AI-powered robots to automate fashion e-commerce returns. These robotic systems handle tasks from unpacking garments to inspecting their condition and determining their next step. The AI assesses clothing items to decide if they are suitable for resale, repair, or recycling, addressing the complexity of varied garment shapes and conditions. This technology aims to help retailers manage surplus inventory in response to environmental regulations. Other robotics companies are already applying similar AI solutions to fashion retailer returns.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, Neuryn Robotics develops AI-powered robots to automate fashion returns, a development focused on streamlining the processing of returned apparel. Neuryn Robotics, a startup based in Madrid, is currently developing robotic systems designed to automate the entire process of fashion e-commerce returns. These robotic systems are engineered to handle tasks ranging from the unpacking of garments to the detailed inspection of their condition and subsequent determination of the appropriate next action. The artificial intelligence within these systems assesses clothing items to categorize them for resale, repair, or recycling, effectively managing the complexity introduced by varied garment shapes and conditions. This technology is intended to assist retailers in managing surplus inventory in compliance with environmental regulations. Other robotics entities are also implementing comparable artificial intelligence solutions for managing fashion retailer returns. This advancement indicates a growing application of sophisticated AI in the logistics and sustainability sectors.

items.title: TÜV SÜD awards human-machine performance certification to Ascentiz exoskeletons
items.summary: TÜV SÜD awarded Human-Machine Performance Certification to Ascentiz's Pro and Ultra modular hip exoskeletons. The certification resulted from independent testing across various performance indicators, including workload reduction, fatigue relief, range, and noise levels. Testing involved seven everyday activities, showing significant exertion decrease, such as over 44 percent reduction in muscle group exertion during uphill walking. The exoskeletons demonstrated a travel range exceeding 6 km under demanding conditions and a peak hip extension torque of approximately 22.5 Nm per side. This certification recognizes Ascentiz's commitment to user experience and provides an independent assessment for the consumer exoskeleton industry.

items.title: Path2 develops online robot cell builder to make automation more accessible
items.summary: Path2 is developing a browser-based platform to allow smaller manufacturers to design and program robot workcells without large integration budgets. Users can virtually position robots, conveyors, and safety guards, and teach robot movements on screen to generate programs automatically. A demonstration showed a layout to a running palletizing cycle in just 19 minutes with no manual code writing. The platform currently supports 20 Kuka robot models and plans to expand to other major manufacturers. Path2 will also offer engineering packages and guide users through machinery safety processes, with pricing structured around design packages and subscriptions.

items.title: ROS Discourse General: Ramp Autonomy: a ROS 2 / Gazebo stack for ramp ascent and descent on a loaded AMR
items.summary: A ROS 2/Gazebo stack is presented for ramp ascent and descent on a loaded AMR using Nav2 MPPI control. The system addresses the issue where standard navigation assumes flat ground, which fails on ramps due to IMU bias, shifting center of gravity, and wheel slip. The framework employs a five-state Finite State Machine, a LiDAR slope classifier, and safety layers to manage these dynamics. The author shares specific findings regarding MPPI profile asymmetry and the impact of speed capping on wheel slip during descent. The project is currently simulated, and the author seeks feedback on parameter tuning and real-world validation.
items.audio_script: From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: Ramp Autonomy: a ROS 2 / Gazebo stack for ramp ascent and descent on a loaded AMR". This story details a ROS 2 and Gazebo stack developed for ramp ascent and descent on a loaded Autonomous Mobile Robot. The system successfully addresses navigation challenges encountered on inclines by managing IMU bias, center of gravity shifts, and wheel slip. The framework utilizes a five-state Finite State Machine, integrates a LiDAR slope classifier, and incorporates safety layers to handle the dynamic changes during traversal. Specific findings included observations regarding MPPI profile asymmetry and the effect of speed capping on wheel slip during descent. This research contributes to the development of more robust navigation systems for mobile robotics in complex environments.

items.title: Knitting a New Future for Robot Fashion
items.summary: CMU and Kent State students collaborated to win a $2,000 prize at the Humanoid Robot Fashion Challenge. The winning team designed an outfit for a humanoid robot using computational textile design to explore functional and movable garments. Students integrated skills from textile design, coding, and fashion to create the ensemble. This challenge highlighted the importance of how robots will be perceived through their appearance and interaction with people. The winning designs will be featured at a Robot Fashion event during New York Fashion Week.

The winning team utilized computational textile design to develop an outfit for a humanoid robot, exploring functional and movable garments by integrating skills from textile design, coding, and fashion. This process highlighted the significance of how robots will be perceived based on their visual appearance and interaction with human observers. items.title: Zipline and Chipotle complete first drone food delivery in PGA Tour history
items.summary: Zipline and Chipotle achieved the first drone food delivery in PGA Tour history by delivering meals to two professional golfers during a practice round in Austin, Texas. The delivery involved drones dropping food directly onto the golf course for golfers Joel Dahmen and Mark Hubbard. Dahmen received a steak bowl, and Hubbard received a steak burrito with guacamole. Chipotle partnered with Zipline to expand delivery capabilities to unconventional locations like golf courses, available in Dallas and Austin. This event demonstrates the potential of autonomous aerial delivery systems for novel delivery scenarios.

items.title: EvoMisty: Building, Optimizing, and Evolving Capabilities on a Social Robot
items.summary: EvoMisty is a framework designed to build, optimize, and evolve the capabilities of social robots through a plugin-based approach. It enables coding agents to construct control programs from documentation and verify capabilities on physical robots, storing verified skills in an atomic library. The system collects execution data, measures user-specified metrics, and iteratively improves task programs. EvoMisty distills reusable skills from successful solutions into a skill library for future use. Experiments showed that optimization significantly improved performance metrics, such as reducing dialogue response latency by up to 71%.

items.title: Learning from Human Corrections through Temporal Preferences
items.summary: Human corrections provide information through both the nature of the correction and the timing of the intervention. The work proposes using both pre- and post-intervention behaviors to form preference pairs for learning value functions that approximate a human's latent reward. Post-intervention preferences derived from comparing corrected versus replaced behavior are effective for goal inference. Pre-intervention preferences, based on temporal state relationships, show strong performance for correction forecasting. Combining both temporal and comparative preferences results in strong performance across both downstream tasks.

items.title: Geometric Control Analysis of an Internally Actuated Flying Wing
items.summary: A geometric control analysis was performed for a fixed-wing Uncrewed Aircraft System actuated by an internal moving mass, a momentum wheel, and external thrust. This method eliminates traditional control surfaces, simplifying high-fidelity modeling of unsteady flow fields. Lie bracket computations demonstrate that the full nonlinear dynamics are generically small-time locally accessible. The momentum wheel and mass inertia variations allow for full-rank accessibility in the Lie algebra. A nonlinear Model Predictive Controller is subsequently derived for trajectory tracking under various flow conditions.

items.title: CRAB-H: Task-Centric Certification for Healthcare Autonomous Systems
items.summary: CRAB-H introduces a task-centric certification methodology for healthcare autonomous systems by making the task a first-class governance object via Task Requirement Profiles (TRP H). This method assesses certification by comparing demonstrated capabilities against required task capabilities, rather than just benchmark scores. A reliability-gated assurance allocation mechanism handles unevaluable cognitive dimensions by routing them to operational requirements. Governance integrity is maintained by governing unreliable dimensions rather than ignoring them. The Capability Margin is determined by threshold-based compliance, preserving necessary non-compensatory safety logic.

items.title: Embodied Neuro-symbolic AI: Making Robot Behavior Auditable, Safe, and Scalable
items.summary: Vision-Language-Action systems struggle with generalization, physical reasoning, and fine-grained control in real-world robot deployment. Embodied Neuro-symbolic (NeSy) AI is proposed as a paradigm to address these issues by integrating learned perception with explicit, machine-readable background knowledge and formal constraints. This approach uses knowledge-guided perception and constraint-aware planning to allow robots to reason about their environment. Consequently, Embodied NeSy AI enables robots to exhibit behavior that is auditable and verifiable regarding safety and operational requirements. This methodology supports the development of scalable and trustworthy robot systems.

items.title: Hi3R-VLA: Grounding Semantics and Actions in 3D
items.summary: Hi3R-VLA is a 3D policy designed to ground vision, language, and action modalities in explicit 3D geometry for robotic manipulation. It integrates spatially-aligned visual features and language conditioning into point cloud representations to enrich scene geometry with task-relevant semantics. The model anchors control commands in the same 3D frame and uses 3D-RoPE enhanced attention to model geometric relationships between action targets and observed points. Analysis shows that semantic fusion within 3D and spatial alignment between observations and actions are crucial. Hi3R-VLA achieves state-of-the-art performance across various manipulation tasks with under 250M trainable parameters.

items.title: Sampling at Scale: Distributed Multi-Agent Trajectory Optimization
items.summary: Multi-agent trajectory optimization faces challenges in exploring non-convex landscapes and scaling to large teams. The proposed method introduces a Distributed Sampling-based Trajectory Optimization (DS-TO) architecture using a splitting mechanism. This allows each agent to sample only in its control space, independently of neighborhood size, while still considering other agents' decisions. The algorithm is fully decentralized, relying only on neighborhood communication for parallel local updates. Experiments show improved exploration and constraint satisfaction over other methods for large agent teams.

items.title: FabricBench: A Standardized Policy Benchmark for Bimanual Fabric Manipulation with a Contact-Driven Deformable Simulator
items.summary: FabricBench introduces a benchmark for bimanual fabric manipulation using a contact-driven deformable simulator. It features six tasks involving garments, silk, and bags, with 10,000 simulation-ready assets. The simulator allows stable grasping and release through contact forces, enabling interactions between robot arms and fabric. Evaluation of various policies shows challenges, with the best policy achieving 77% success but falling to under 36% on long-horizon folding tasks. The benchmark serves as a reproducible testbed for measuring fabric manipulation capabilities and generalization limits.

items.title: A Self-Organizing Swarm Control Model for Underwater Robots Based on Turing-Type Reaction-Diffusion Principles
items.summary: The model proposes a decentralized swarm control for underwater robots operating without GPS or reliable communication. It utilizes Turing-type reaction-diffusion principles, extending a cellular automaton to continuous space, to govern swarm behavior. Swarm formation is driven by robots moving towards regions of higher potential calculated from signal differences between inner and outer neighborhoods. Stable behavior is achieved through temporal averaging, hysteresis-based evaluation, and stepwise turning. Simulations confirm the model's ability to autonomously form and control the spatial dispersion of the swarm, even with reduced communication success rates.

items.title: Collision Rendering: GPU-Accelerated Trajectory Planning on Sparse Voxel Radiance Fields with Risk-Bounded Collision Checking
items.summary: Collision Rendering introduces a framework for trajectory planning on sparse voxel radiance fields by leveraging GPU acceleration. It achieves this through risk-bounded collision checking and a differentiable collision cost derived from rendering pipelines. The method approximates the robot as collision spheres, using rendering to estimate collision probability bounds. This results in a modular collision checker that integrates with sampling-based planners without needing extra geometric maps. Experiments show millisecond collision checking and successful trajectory planning on consumer GPUs.
